title: Negative: the proposed fix for an honest dividing crawler (capped area term, actin paid from content, low food stock) gives a transient crawl-divide-starve phase, then a static remnant or a churning sea
summary: First test of the experiment in 20261025T1014-c04-q-honest-metabolic-crawler, world.py here (cdiv with okclip=1, bV=1, shed=0, kup=0.05, n0=0.5; new switches capdev caps |A-V| in delta at capdev, kact charges content for actin production kact*int|P|^2), seed 1 unless noted, t=600. capdev 0.3, kact 0.1 (v2b/): crawling crescents grow, tear and divide until t~340 and small starving cells shrink to dots and vanish (genuine intrinsic deaths, sheet t=420-575), then 3 round static cells remain; labkit max generation 2, max 1.5 body lengths at 2.5 time units per frame (fast crescents may be undercounted). kact 0.05 (v2a/): 12 bodies peak, 1 left, generation 2; capdev 0.15 (v2c/): peak 20, extinct. Raising regrowth to rn 0.004 or 0.008 (v2r*/, seeds 1-2) gives a crowded churning population (merge/split 0.62-0.85, no persistent splits, <= 1.3 body lengths except one 4.2) or a single domain-filling body (occupancy 0.96). So with growth paid honestly and costs on motion, this model has either a transient phase or a sea; I found no regime with sustained crawling division.

finding.operator: content-paid actin with a capped area-deficit term
finding.result: transient crawl-divide-starve phase to t~340 then static remnant (v2b); extinction or a churning sea elsewhere; max generation <= 2
